claim: Jefferies downgraded Apple from Hold to Underperform (PT $263.66) on August 10, 2026, citing rising memory costs and reports the all-glass iPhone redesign was cancelled; the second leg was contradicted within 24 hours by a Bloomberg report saying the redesign remains on track for 2027.
stance_target: bear case built on the all-glass iPhone cancellation narrative
scope_conditions: August 2026, Jefferies analyst call vs Bloomberg reporting
quoted_support: "A Bloomberg report on August 11 says Apple's glass-centric iPhone Pro redesign remains on track for the 2027 20th anniversary. That directly contradicts the cancellation narrative Jefferies used to justify slashing its target."

claim: Apple's operating income grew 26.57% YoY in FQ3 2026, outpacing 16.4% revenue growth, indicating margin leverage rather than compression despite memory cost inflation.
stance_target: bear case that memory costs are compressing Apple's margins
quoted_support: "Operating income expanded 26.57% year over year, outpacing revenue growth. That is margin leverage, not compression."

claim: Supply-chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo argues the memory-cost 'panic' is overstated because Apple plans processor production months in advance, making any acute shock scenario unlikely.
stance_target: bear case that memory-cost inflation poses an acute margin risk
quoted_support: "Tight memory supply is real," yet Apple plans processor production months in advance, making any shock scenario unlikely.
